title: Finite-cover model with two Cartier boundary complements
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T$ a nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $S\subseteq T^\circ\subseteq T$ dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $c:H\to S$ be a nonempty finite etale surjection [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Write $K=k(T)$ [def-sc-function-field], choose a point $x$ of $H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and put $F=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The extension $F/K$ is finite [def-pc-field-extension]. There exist a normal integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ and a finite surjective $k$-morphism $q:X\to T$ with function field $F$, where $q$ is the normalization of $T$ in $F$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Normal means that each local ring is an integrally closed domain. Moreover, there exist an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B$ and a proper dominant $k$-morphism $b:B\to X$ inducing an isomorphism $k(X)\simeq k(B)$ compatible with $k(T)$, such that $b^{-1}(q^{-1}S)\to q^{-1}S$ is an isomorphism and $q^{-1}S\to S$ factors through $c$. There are effective Cartier ideals $\mathcal I_B,\mathcal J_B\subseteq\mathcal O_B$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] satisfying
$$V(\mathcal I_B)=B\setminus(qb)^{-1}S,\qquad V(\mathcal J_B)=B\setminus(qb)^{-1}T^\circ.$$
The composite $g=qb:B\to T$ is proper dominant, $k(B)=F$ over $K$, and $g^{-1}S\to S$ factors through $c$. Unit ideals and identity modifications are allowed when a complement is empty.

proof.text: The projection p : H ×_S Spec K → Spec K is etale. Its residue-field map at x is etale by the etale residue-field-map tool. The canonical residue-point map into Spec K is an isomorphism (it is a surjective closed immersion into a reduced one-point scheme). Thus Spec κ(x) → Spec K is etale for precisely the algebra installed by coverGenericResidueAlgebra. Algebra.FormallyUnramified.finite_of_free gives Module.Finite K κ(x), equivalently FiniteDimensional. This is the finite-field clause of the original etale-fibre step; no discreteness or chosen field-factor decomposition is needed.

Put F = κ(x), X = T.normalizationIn F and q = T.fromNormalizationIn F. The relative normalization of the integral scheme Spec F is integral. Its stalks are integrally closed by normalization-normal-stalks, since the stalk of Spec F is F. Finiteness of q is isFinite_fromNormalizationIn applied to t. The canonical Spec F → T contains the generic point in its image and is dominant; its normalization factorization makes q dominant. Since q is finite, it is proper and closed, hence surjective. The generic-field theorem supplies the specified eX and its commuting equation.

Separatedness, local finite type, and quasi-compactness of q followed by t follow by the existing composition instances. Every blowup used below is proper; the same composition instances give these properties for its structure map. LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian gives local Noetherianity over the field at X and at the first blowup.

Let f : Spec F → T be the canonical generic field morphism and a₀ : Spec F → H the residue-point morphism followed by the first projection. Spec.homEquiv and the pullback equation give f = a₀ c S.ι. Normalization commutes with the smooth base change S.ι. For p = pullback.snd f S.ι the first projection followed by a₀ factors p through the integral morphism c. Apply normalizationDesc, then compose with the inverse normalizationPullback and the restriction pullback isomorphism. The normalizationDesc_comp and normalizationPullback_snd equations give a : q⁻¹S → H with a c = q|S.

Set U = q⁻¹S and V = q⁻¹Tcirc. The first is nonempty by density of S and surjectivity of q, and U ≤ V. Use the locally Noetherian complement-ideal theorem to obtain a finite-type ideal A with support X minus U. It is nonzero since U is nonempty. Its blowup X₁ is integral by isIntegral_blowup_and_isProjectiveBundle, and proper by isProper_blowupMap. The complement theorem makes it an isomorphism over U. Principalization makes A₁ = A O_X₁ invertible. The comap support equation identifies its support with X₁ minus b₁⁻¹U.

The inverse image U₁ of U in X₁ is nonempty because b₁ is an isomorphism there. Put V₁ = b₁⁻¹V. Use the locally Noetherian complement-ideal theorem again to obtain C supported on X₁ minus V₁. It is nonzero because U₁ is nonempty and U₁ ≤ V₁. Its blowup B is integral and b₂ is proper. C is disjoint from U₁, so b₂ is an isomorphism over U₁. Set J = C O_B; principalization makes it invertible and comap support gives support B minus (b₂b₁)⁻¹V.
Set I = A₁ O_B. Cartier total transform under b₂ makes I invertible. Applying the comap support equation twice identifies its support with B minus (b₂b₁)⁻¹U.

Set b = b₂ followed by b₁. Restriction commutes with composition, so b|U is an isomorphism. Since U is a nonempty open of integral X it is dense, and surjectivity of b|U shows U is contained in the image of b; hence b is dominant. Write W = b⁻¹U. W is nonempty and integral. Both W.ι : W → B and W.ι followed by b : W → X are open immersions. Their generic stalk isomorphisms (functionFieldIso) give Spec k(X) ≅ Spec k(W) ≅ Spec k(B). Naturality of fromSpecStalk gives the required commuting equation with b. This construction also covers empty boundary complements without a special branch.

Properness of b and of g = b followed by q, dominance of g, and the finite-type separated structure map of B follow by composition. The support equations above are definitionally the requested equations after substituting U and V. The map a : q⁻¹S → H supplied by normalization factors q|S through c. Compose it with b|q⁻¹S; the restriction-composition identity gives a factorization of g|S through c. Assemble the normality, finite normalization, generic isomorphisms, proper modification and boundary clauses.

Step 2: the residue-field normalization lemma (T quasi-separated, so normal integral X with generic point Spec F), finite by lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite, then proper and closed, so surjective. Step 3 is a genuinely elementary diagonal composition. Step 4: q^{-1}S is the normalization of S in Spec F (035K, morphisms.tex l.14039); the qcqs and integral-c hypotheses hold, and the universal property gives U->H with no normality of S or H needed. Step 5: qcqs plus Noetherian with DCC, so every open is quasi-compact, which are exactly the hypotheses of the complement-ideal and boundary-divisor nodes. Steps 6-7: nonzero ideals (unit on a nonempty open) give integral blowups that are proper, isomorphisms over U and V_1, with invertible extended ideals of the right support (02OS l.8383). Step 8: total transform (0809 l.8567) plus support V(aO_B)=b_2^{-1}V(a). Step 9: compositions, generic stalks give k(B)=F over K, and the factorization.
